rejected.detail: Test passes identically at base and merge (23 passed, 10 pg-infra errors both times); PR's own message says 'mechanism unchanged since pass 6' — no discriminating red.

environment_notes: Python 3.10.6 venv at scratchpad/ecorpus-rb/venv with restaurant-brain's runtime deps only (pip install -e '.[dev]' then `pip uninstall restaurant-brain` to strip the editable install, which otherwise shadows worktree app/ code via a meta-path finder). Disclosure on the one command that touched the actual repo checkout: the initial `pip install -e '.[dev]'` was run from the user's real working tree (before any worktree existed) to resolve dependencies; it only refreshed the pre-existing, gitignored restaurant_brain.egg-info/ directory — `git status --short` was empty immediately after, confirmed again at the very end of the session. No file inside the real checkout was created, modified, or committed at any point. Most tests use the db_session fixture (in-memory SQLite via StaticPool) — no external services needed. tests/test_auth_card8.py and part of tests/test_schema_drift_check.py require live Postgres (pg_session/live_pg_engine fixtures, which FAIL LOUD rather than skip if unreachable); `docker compose up -d db` (postgres:16-alpine, host port 5434) plus TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgresql+psycopg://brain:brain@localhost:5434/restaurant_brain satisfies this — used once, for PR 369, then torn down (`docker compose down`) before finishing; no repo files were touched by this either (docker-compose.yml was only read). Reproduction method: for each PR, two `git worktree add --detach` checkouts (base=merge^1, merge=mergeCommit) under scratchpad/ecorpus-rb/; RED is measured by running the MERGE worktree's test file against the BASE worktree's app/ (and scripts/, content/, demo/, guardrails/ if present) via a third scratch dir of symlinks (app,scripts,... -> base; tests,pyproject.toml -> merge) so pytest's own sys.path rootdir-insertion can't accidentally pick up the fixed app code (a plain PYTHONPATH-ordering trick failed for this reason — pytest prepends the test file's package root before PYTHONPATH). GREEN is a plain pytest run inside the merge worktree. Harness self-check: reran PR 461's RED farm with app symlinked to MERGE instead of base (everything else identical) and got 4 passed, matching the plain merge-worktree run exactly — this confirms the farm layout itself is not what's producing RED, isolating the app-code swap as the actual cause for the whole family of PRs built this way. All worktrees and scratch symlink dirs were removed after each PR (including the control run); main repo working tree confirmed clean (git status) at the end. Several 'new test file in the same PR as the fix' cases (442, 423, 422) mean RED is technically 'apply the PR's test to base app code' rather than 'run an unmodified pre-existing test against base' — this is the standard SWE-bench-style FAIL_TO_PASS reproduction and was necessary because most of the 37 candidates add their test file in the same PR as the fix. RED_KIND is recorded per admissible entry (assertion / runtime-typeerror / collection-error) since a collection-error RED (422, 423) means the derived task is 'write from scratch', not 'fix a bug' — worth filtering on downstream.
